runscript.name: SR75 HIL-F24-R1 dynamic state feed (ground-static, engines off)
runscript.description:
HIL-F24-R1: continuous live SR-75 6-DOF JSBSim state for feeding the real Pixhawk over PPP/SIM_JSON in MANUAL/disarmed mode.
Ground-level, motionless start (accel_ground_init, the same IC used by the validated SR75_accel_ground_test.xml accelerometer-semantics test). All engines are explicitly held off and RATO/turbojet/flight control commands are pinned at zero for the entire run: this simulation never produces engine, RATO, or actuator output; it only ever supplies read-only 6-DOF state to sr75_hil_f24r1_dynamic_jsbsim_feed.py, which republishes it as an atomic state.csv snapshot for sr75_sim_json_responder.py (LOG_ONLY actuator mode, no jsbsim-command-target option) to answer the Pixhawk's SIM_JSON requests with. No JSBSim property is ever written to based on anything the Pixhawk sends: there is no feedback path into this simulation at all in HIL-F24-R1.
Every output field below is named to match sr75_hil_f24d_static_state_feed.py's CSV_FIELDS exactly (and thus StateMapper.state_from_csv()'s recognized column names in sr75_sim_json_responder.py), in SI units, so the Python feeder needs no unit conversion of its own: only a straight column-matched passthrough into atomic_write_csv_snapshot().
A long run end (3600s) is used deliberately; the actual test duration is controlled externally by the Python feeder terminating this JSBSim subprocess, the same way sr75_hil_f24d_static_state_feed.py's own duration-s option controls the static feeder's run length.

event.name: Engines off, RATO/throttle/controls pinned at zero for the whole run
